doc.title: Peter Ecklund interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998

title: Building a personal style: classical roots, Bix and Armstrong
summary: He describes improvising as building a personal language, his classical-only background, the friend's father's record collection, and his admiration for Bix Beiderbecke and Louis Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: You mentioned Wild Bill Davison and I wonder, do you fit yourself into a line of trumpet players do you think? Were there people that you listened to when you were coming up learning the instrument, that became part of your sound?

Oh yeah. I mean every musician who plays improvised music goes through this, I mean you have to in order to — improvising, creating an improvising style is kind of like creating your personal language. And you have to kind of put together your vocabulary. It’s kind of a language that only you speak. And you put it together out of various things that you hear around you. And so sure, I mean I played nothing but classical music until I was almost finished with college. But I always listened to a lot of jazz, traditional jazz and like Miles Davis and like that. And I got interested in traditional jazz because the father of a friend of mine had a very good record collection and was interested in that, and my friend played trombone, and he played trumpet. And he had played with Rudy Vallee’s orchestra back in the 1920s so he knew a lot of those old songs and like that.
Was there one particular person, a jazz trumpeter that made you really sit up and say that’s somebody I’d really like to sound like? © Fiillius Jazz Archive -3-
Well I guess I liked Bix Beiderbecke and Louis Armstrong back in those days, and of course I still do now.

I had a feeling you might say that, listening to what you play, that I could hear that in your sound. Can you explain — this is always a tough question — in fact you came through the classical school.
